To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 36Ca nucleus has been identified by γ decay of its 2+ excited state, the 2+ excitation energy is 3015(15) keV.

the MED within a T = 1 sd shell pair is a sensitive probe for the evolution of shell gaps towards the dripline and the N, Z > 16 subshell closure is determined by the Thomas–Ehrmann shift in the A, T = 1 17 isospin doublets.
the 36Ca(2+)→ 36Ca(0+) MED of 276± 16 keV, which we determined by means of the γ decay of the first excited state, is lower than the corresponding MED in the T=2 mirror 36S.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the nuclear shell structure towards the drip lines, and with the isospin symmetry at extreme proton and neutron number.
the structure of nuclei at the proton drip-line, where nuclei are unstable with respect to proton emission.
the study of nuclear structure and reactions in the vicinity of the proton and neutron drip lines, where the nuclear binding energy is small and the nuclear density is large.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N, Z=16 shell gaps are not yet reached for 36 Ca and 36 S, and that the N,Z=14 shell gaps are only reached for 36 S, but not for 36 Ca.

, for the sd shell, the isospin symmetry is broken by the Thomas–Ehrmann effect in the N = Z + 1, T = 0 mirror pair 36 S and 36 Ar and in the N = 2, T = 3/2 mirror pairs 37 Ca and 37 K, while it is not broken in the N =Z, T = 2 and the N = Z− 2, T=−2 mirror pairs 36 Ca

the experimental data are in very good agreement with the predictions of shell-model calculations using the USD interaction and experimental single-particles energies from the T = 1 / 2 mirror nuclei 17 O, 17 F, and 17 Ne.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MED within sd-shell mirror pairs provide a sensitive test on the evolution of subshell gaps towards driplines.
we have shown the first excited 2+ state in the Tz=-2 nucleus 36Ca and that it decays with a half-life of about 0.6 ns.
we have identified the first excited 2+ state in the Tz = −2 nucleus 36Ca and measured a mirror energy difference (ME) between 36Ca and its T = 1 mirror 36S.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have measured for the first time a γ -ray transition in a T = 2 nucleus at the dripline and that we have found a large MED between its mirror partners.
we have observed the first excited state of 36Ca, and that this is the heaviest nucleus for which a γ decay of an excited state is observed.
shell model calculations using the USD interaction with the 16 O core reproduce the experimental data on the T = 2 mirrors 36 Ca and 36 S.
